title: AI Adoption: What the 2026 Data Actually Shows

caption.text:
Most AI adoption decks fail for a boring reason: they present ambition as evidence.

This one is eight slides of published data, with the source printed on every page.

The short version:

1. Format matters more than volume — LinkedIn document posts still out-engage every other organic format.
2. Depth beats reach — dwell time is the metric the ranking system rewards.
3. Provenance is the differentiator — a cited number survives a skeptical executive, an adjective does not.

If your team is building an adoption case this quarter, start with the measurement, not the roadmap.

Which of the three findings is hardest to get internal agreement on?

sources: Buffer, State of Social Engagement, March 2026 (52M+ posts)

slides.kicker: Eight pages, three findings, zero adjectives.
slides.headline: AI adoption: what the data actually shows
slides.sub: A measurement-first brief for teams building an adoption case this quarter.
slides.alt_text: Cover page of a LinkedIn benchmark brief on AI adoption.

slides.headline: Format still beats volume on LinkedIn
slides.metric_label: Engagement by impressions, native document posts
slides.finding: Document posts lead every other LinkedIn organic format and rose year over year, while the platform average stayed flat. The variable is not posting frequency — it is whether the format rewards time on post.
slides.alt_text: Proof page showing 7.00% engagement for LinkedIn document posts.

slides.headline: The gap is dwell time, not reach
slides.takeaway: Engagement by impressions across LinkedIn organic formats.
slides.alt_text: Horizontal bar chart of LinkedIn engagement by format.

slides.headline: Reach-weighted, documents look even stronger
slides.metric_label: Median engagement by reach, document posts
slides.finding: Measured against unique reach rather than impressions, documents roughly triple the engagement rate of video in the same cohort. This is the number to quote when someone asks whether the format is worth the production time.
slides.source: Buffer, State of Social Engagement, March 2026 — 52M+ posts
slides.alt_text: Proof page showing 21.77% median engagement by reach for document posts.

slides.headline: Three moves that survive scrutiny
slides.alt_text: Bento grid of four adoption moves: measure, publish depth, cite, ship weekly.

slides.headline: A four-week pilot you can defend

steps.title: Week 1 — baseline
steps.detail: Pull 90 days of first-party reach and dwell.

steps.title: Week 2 — publish two briefs
steps.detail: Five to eight pages, sourced on every page.

steps.title: Week 3 — compare cohorts
steps.detail: Same audience, same offer, format as the only variable.

steps.title: Week 4 — decide with a number
steps.detail: Scale, iterate, or kill it. Write down which.

slides.alt_text: Four-step pilot plan spanning four weeks.
